items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: I thought that Louis got a lot from Bunk... When I first heard Bunk, I was a kid around nine or ten years old... Bunk was the radiest trumpet player at that time in New Orleans... This man was really great.

ctx.x: You were talking about Armstrong, Albert. Yeah. And remember you saying the other day that you thought that Louis got a lot from Bunk and those more recent records made in American music by Bunk, you didn't feel were really Bunk in his prime. Obviously they weren't because he was getting on years. Could you tell us a bit about Bunk? You heard Bunk in New Orleans.

When I first heard Bunk, I was a kid around nine or ten years old. He was playing with the Superior Band. Maggill was playing with the Imperial. Bunk was the radiest trumpet player at that time in New Orleans, what we call Gut Bucket later on. He was a kid around nine or ten years old. He was a writer. And Bunk had ideas. It's too bad that they weren't recording in those times. This man was really great. And I heard the old man again in 45, after being in retirement for 20-some years, and 60-some years of age. He…
Would you say that that band that was recorded in 42, 43, 44, the Bunk band, it was the same as Bunk was playing around about 1918?
